review:
SUMMARY: Two confirmed issues in the permission annotation rollout: a read-only permission incorrectly guarding a write endpoint, and a custom exception inheriting from a misaligned Bean Validation base class.

POINTS:
- [core/src/main/java/io/aiven/klaw/controller/TopicController.java:307] POST /saveTopicDocumentation is guarded by VIEW_TOPICS, allowing read-only users to modify topic documentation — fix: change to PermissionType.REQUEST_EDIT_TOPICS
- [core/src/main/java/io/aiven/klaw/error/PermissionConstraintException.java:6] Extends ConstraintDeclarationException, causing runtime authorization failures to be incorrectly caught as Bean Validation configuration errors

suspicions.observation: PermissionConstraintException extends ConstraintDeclarationException, which is a Bean Validation exception intended for constraint declaration/configuration problems at startup (e.g., invalid annotation usage), not for runtime authorization failures.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Any existing or future code that catches ConstraintDeclarationException expecting it to mean "constraint is misconfigured" will incorrectly catch and handle permission denials as configuration errors. This is a semantic misuse of the parent exception class.

suspicions.observation: POST endpoint /saveTopicDocumentation is annotated with @PermissionAllowed(permissionAllowed = {PermissionType.VIEW_TOPICS}). This is a write operation (saves documentation) that only requires a read/view permission.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Any user with VIEW_TOPICS permission can modify topic documentation despite only having a "view" permission. Write operations should require a higher/dedicated permission, not a read-only permission.

suspicions.observation: Method name is handlePermissionNotAuthoirzedExceptionInternal - "Authoirzed" is misspelled (should be "Authorized").
suspicions.suspected_bug: Typo in method name - minor cosmetic issue but could cause confusion during debugging.

suspicions.observation: BuildProperties is imported and autowired (line 85: @Autowired BuildProperties buildProperties;) but never used anywhere in the test class.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Dead code - unused autowired field in test class.

suspicions.observation: The PR introduces an @Aspect-based permission interceptor (PermissionAllowedAspectInterceptor) as the sole permission enforcement mechanism, but the project has NO spring-boot-starter-aop dependency in pom.xml and NO @EnableAspectJAutoProxy annotation anywhere. This is the only @Aspect class in the entire codebase. Spring Boot does not enable AspectJ auto-proxying by default without the AOP starter.
suspicions.suspected_bug: The @Before("@annotation(permissionAllowed)") advice will NEVER execute because Spring AOP/AspectJ is not configured. The @PermissionAllowed annotations are completely inert. Combined with the removal of existing permission checks from the service layer, this means ALL permission enforcement on Topic and Connector endpoints is silently bypassed - any authenticated user can perform any Topic/Connector operation regardless of their permissions.

bugs.observation: POST endpoint /saveTopicDocumentation is annotated with @PermissionAllowed(permissionAllowed = {PermissionType.VIEW_TOPICS}). This is a write operation (saves documentation) that only requires a read/view permission.
bugs.suspected_bug: Any user with VIEW_TOPICS permission can modify topic documentation despite only having a "view" permission. Write operations should require a higher/dedicated permission, not a read-only permission.
bugs.evidence: TopicController.java:307 - @PermissionAllowed(permissionAllowed = {PermissionType.VIEW_TOPICS}) on saveTopicDocumentation allows any user with VIEW_TOPICS (a read-only permission) to modify topic documentation via a POST endpoint, which is a security issue. The test correctly asserts that a write operation must not use only VIEW_TOPICS permission.

solutions.fix_diff:
The production fix was correct: changed PermissionConstraintException from extending ConstraintDeclarationException (a Bean Validation config exception) to extending RuntimeException (a proper runtime authorization exception). This correctly addresses the semantic misuse described in the bug.

However, the test has a design flaw in `catchingConstraintDeclarationExceptionMustNotCatchPermissionException`:
- It throws a PermissionConstraintException inside a try-catch that only catches ConstraintDeclarationException
- If PermissionConstraintException extends RuntimeException (correct fix), the exception is NOT caught by the catch block, but it also propagates out of the method, causing the test to ERROR (not PASS)
- If PermissionConstraintException extends ConstraintDeclarationException (buggy state), the catch block catches it, caught=true, and the assertion FAILS

The test cannot pass with production-only changes because the uncaught exception propagates, making the test error. The test needs an additional catch block (e.g., `catch (Exception e) {}` or `catch (RuntimeException e) {}`) to properly handle the case where the exception doesn't extend ConstraintDeclarationException.
